subject: Client education
label: BEFORE YOU HIRE
caption_ig:
Stop paying for a website redesign just because your current one looks old. Fix the broken funnel first. 

#webdesign #smallbusiness #conversionrate #entrepreneur #webstrategy
caption_fb: When business owners decide they need a website redesign, the reason is usually that the current site feels dated. But focusing purely on aesthetics often misses the real issue. A visual upgrade will not fix an unclear offer or a broken contact form. Before you reach out to a designer, check your analytics to see where customers actually drop off.
caption_li:
The most expensive website redesign is the one that only changes how things look.

Many business owners assume that a fresh layout will automatically bring in better clients. But visual polish only amplifies your underlying message. If visitors still cannot figure out your pricing within seconds, a prettier background will not save the sale.

Before looking for a designer, figure out the specific bottleneck your new site needs to solve.

What metric made you first consider a redesign?

slides.title: Is your site dated or broken?
slides.body: A new coat of paint will not fix low sales if your checkout page crashes or your contact form goes straight to spam.

slides.title: Pretty layouts do not fix weak offers.
slides.body: Upgrading fonts and colors will not attract better clients if visitors cannot figure out what you sell within five seconds.

slides.title: Design amplifies your message, good or bad.
slides.body: If your current page confuses people, a slick new redesign just makes a confusing message look more expensive.

slides.title: Find the leak before hiring a designer.
slides.body: Check your analytics. Are people leaving because pricing is hidden, or because the booking link takes three clicks too many?

slides.title: Pay to solve friction, not boredom.
slides.body: Write down the exact business problem your new site must fix before you waste money on pure aesthetics.
